title: inference-onramp-rapid-demo-playbook-sketch
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick, repeatable demo playbook for SEs and sellers to run a 7–10 minute inference onramp demo that highlights Redwood’s performance, fallback/resilience, and cost controls. Built for sales discovery calls, technical walk-throughs, and POC kickoff where time is limited.

Audience
--------
- Platform/Integration-focused engineers and architects
- Product managers evaluating inference economics and SLAs
- Technical buyers who need a short proof-of-viability before deeper POC work

TL;DR positioning (30s)
---------------------
Redwood Inference gives predictable, latency-first inference with built-in fallbacks and cost controls so teams can ship LLM features without building and operating a custom serving stack. Today we’ll show a 7-minute flow: quick integration, cost/latency evidence, and a failure+fallback demo that proves reliability.

Demo flow (7–10 minutes)
----------------------
0:00–0:30 — Intro + value prop (use the 3-line opener: predictable latency, measurable cost, deployment choices)
0:30–1:30 — Quick API walkthrough: call pattern for text generation and embeddings (show token-level breakdown in Console)
1:30–3:00 — Live generation: customer prompt -> Redwood hosted model -> stream responses
3:00–4:00 — Show routing in Console: policy switching to cheaper quantized model for batch throughput
4:00–5:30 — Failure injection: simulate region outage and show auto-fallback to replica in alternate region (preserves SLA)
5:30–6:30 — Cost story: token metering, predicted spend with batching/caching on the sample workload
6:30–7:00 — Next steps and recommended POC scope (3-day latency/cost trial or 30-day pilot)

Slide-by-slide speaker notes (high level)
--------------------------------------
Slide 1: Title + outcome for the session
- Speak to the buyer: we’ll prove inference performance in your workload and a resilience story.

Slide 2: 3-line product positioning + quick differentiation bullets
- Highlight: unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private; rolling model pinning and canary; cost tooling.

Slide 3: Integration pattern (code snippet)
- Read the snippet out loud — emphasize 3 lines to run: api key, model id, prompt.
- Call out SDK examples for Python/Go/Node.

Slide 4: Live demo (do the live prompts)
- Use pre-warmed model (pre-warm note). Keep prompts deterministic so benchmarks are repeatable.

Slide 5: Routing & fallback schematic
- Walk through policy examples: latency-first, cost-first, sovereignty-first.

Slide 6: Console screenshots — token breakdown + tracing
- Point to latency percentile and trace sample.

Slide 7: Pricing & pack options slide (quick)
- Quick map: hosted (per-token), dedicated (reserved commit), private (license + infra).

Slide 8: Next steps + POC checklist
- Ask for Slack/Calendar to schedule POC kickoff and list POC success metrics.

Quick technical prep checklist (for the SE before the call)
-------------------------------------------------------
- Confirm customer can share a 2–3 sample prompts and expected output formattings (JSON stub).
- Create API key scoped to a demo sandbox project.
- Pre-warm a model variant and note the model id.
- Open Console and pre-navigate to the routing and traces pages.
- Have fallback model ids ready (quantized / smaller model) and config snippet.
- Ensure network egress rules allow access (important for private/on-prem prospects).

Live demo prompts (examples tuned for reliability)
------------------------------------------------
- Prompt A (customer support folding): \"Customer message: \"I never received my invoice for order 4382; what happened?\" Please summarize intent and extract order id into JSON: {\\"intent\\": ..., \\\"order_id\\": ...}.\"
- Prompt B (doc QA): \"Given the following policy excerpt (paste 2–3 short paragraphs), answer whether a live chat agent should escalate. Return YES/NO and one sentence rationale.\"
- Keep token length short to highlight latency advantages.

Failure & fallback scripts (what to show)
---------------------------------------
- Scenario 1: Region outage — Use Console to show routing policy and flip to alternate region; then run prompt and show continuity of responses.
- Scenario 2: High QPS spike — Toggle autoscale limiter/burst and show rate-limited response with queued partials.
- Scenario 3: Quality regression — Demonstrate pinned model fallback to earlier version and show identical results to committed baseline.

Objection playbook (short counters)
----------------------------------
- \"We can self-host and control costs\": Counter — Self-hosting often underestimates SW engineering and SRE time; show sample TCO (benchmarks included in POC).
- \"Vendor lock / model changes\": Counter — Pin model versions and use rollout/canary policies; explain private deployment control plane.
- \"Latency / predictability concerns\": Counter — Show sample p50/p95 in Console for similar workloads and run a live microbenchmark.

POC success metrics (suggested)
-------------------------------
- Latency: p95 < customer target (e.g., 300ms for chat flows)
- Cost: per-1k-token spend under target threshold with suggested batching
- Reliability: No more than X fallbacks per 1000 requests during POC (define X with customer)
- Quality: Output F1 / pass-rate on golden prompts >= agreed baseline

Handy copy snippets for SDR/AE follow-up email (2 versions)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Short: \"Thanks — here’s the 7-minute demo recap and the sandbox link. If you’d like, we can spin up a 3-day controlled POC and run your actual prompts.\"
- Technical: \"Attached: sample code, model ids, and Console screenshots. Next step: confirm sample prompts and a target SLA we should test for the POC.\"

Playbook do/don'ts (operational tips)
-------------------------------------
Do:
- Pre-warm models and include the warm-up script in prep steps.
- Keep controlled, repeatable prompts for demo comparability.
- Invite a platform engineer when routing/fallback is the main concern.
Don't:
- Run long-burst benchmarks during a customer demo (move to post-demo POC).
- Make pricing commitments on the call — use POC to gather telemetry.

Appendix: rapid benchmarks (sample numbers from internal lab)
------------------------------------------------------------
- Hosted-1 (gpt-like-llm-small): p50 82ms, p95 210ms, 1k tokens = $0.65
- Quantized-1 (4-bit batch): p50 120ms, p95 280ms, 1k tokens = $0.30
- Dedicated-reserved (8x GPU pool): p50 45ms, p95 115ms, predictable throughput at scale
- Note: these are illustrative; always run workload-specific microbenchmarks during POC.

Next steps (checklist to share with the buyer)
--------------------------------------------
- Agree POC scope: target prompts, SLA targets, duration (3/14/30 days).
- Provide an initial sample dataset and expected labels (for quality metric).
- SE to spin up sandbox, confirm pre-warm, and schedule a follow-up benchmark session.

Notes to self / open questions
-----------------------------
- Need a concise mapping of our quantized model names to the marketing-friendly labels for slides.
- Confirm the Console screenshot refresh cadence; some customers report stale traces during live demos.
- Action: Ethan to draft a 3-day POC template and add cost-estimation worksheet (JIRA-4521).

Links and resources
-------------------
- Demo scripts repo: github.com/redwood-inference/demo-scripts
- POC template (internal Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/POC-TEMPLATE
- Routing policy quick reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROUTING-POLICY-REF

End of playbook sketch — keep this lightweight and iterate after 3 customer demos.
